key_insight: Confidently wrong LLMs can induce human deference: users absorb false claims with high confidence while their trust in the assistant barely changes.
engineering_relevance: Learning interfaces should make reliability visible claim by claim and evaluate human–AI trust calibration, not just model-side sycophancy.
method: Within-subjects study with 32 participants learning up to five science topics through GPT-5-mini assistants.
Assistant briefings contained 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% plausible falsehoods, all delivered confidently.
Surprise quizzes, answer-confidence ratings, transcript coding, and post-task trust ratings measured uptake and calibration.
evidence_signal: Across 104 quizzes and 1,040 answers, scores fell from 7.4 to 2.9 out of 10; planted falsehoods were selected on 60% of falsified items versus 11% of correctly taught items (odds ratio 12.5).
watch_item: The small, single-model study with deliberately falsified briefings may not generalize to other models or naturally occurring errors.
paper_title: Who Is Sycophantic to Whom? Confident LLMs, Human Deference, and the Collapse of Trust Calibration
